intro.text: On July 1, 2025, Abundia Global Impact Group, Inc. (formerly Houston American Energy Corp.), a Delaware corporation (the “Company”), acquired all of the outstanding units of Abundia Global Impact Group, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“AGIG”), as described below (the “Share Exchange”). Prior to the Share Exchange, the Company operated as an independent oil and gas company, which had previously focused on the development, exploration, exploitation, acquisition, and production of natural gas and crude oil properties, with its principal properties and operations located in the U.S. Permian Basin and additional properties in the Louisiana U.S. Gulf Coast region. The Company intends to continue to maintain its legacy oil and gas assets as well as the AGIG business.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Final product offerings and sales volumes will depend on successful facility development, feedstock availability, regulatory approvals, and customer demand.
Commercial sales are expected to depend on successful facility completion, product qualification and regulatory compliance.

We are designing the facility with the objective of operating as a minor source for purposes of air permitting (i.e., maintaining potential emissions below thresholds that would otherwise trigger more stringent major source and operating permit requirements).

Under past proposals, the EPA would issue or sell a capped and steadily declining number of tradable emissions allowances to certain major sources of greenhouse gas emissions so that such sources could continue to emit greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.
Future capital requirements will depend on many factors, including:
Accordingly, we will need to continue to rely on additional financing to achieve our business objectives.
The Company expects to rely on a limited number of industry partners for a significant portion of its near-term revenue.
The Company and other participants in the alternative energy and fuel industry rely on governmental programs requiring or incentivizing the consumption of low carbon fuels.
Additionally, we must often rely on our own market research to forecast sales, as detailed forecasts are not generally obtainable from other sources at this early stage of the industry.
Our success will depend on our ability to maintain a competitive position with respect to technological advances.

The successful implementation of an expense reduction plan, if and when deemed advisable by management, depends on many factors, including our ability to identify the need for such a plan in a timely manner, to effectively implement such a plan, as well as certain factors which are beyond our control, including economic conditions, labor market conditions and ability to maintain its management team to implement the plan.
We rely on a combination of patent, trademark and trade secret protection, confidentiality, nondisclosure and non-use agreements to protect our proprietary rights.

Additionally, for certain of the Company’s existing and future in-licensed patent rights, it may not have the right to bring suit for infringement and may have to rely on third parties to enforce these rights for it.
We rely on trade secrets to protect some of our technology and proprietary information, especially where we believe patent protection is not appropriate or obtainable.

In addition to the protection afforded by patents, we rely on trade secret protection and confidentiality agreements to protect proprietary know-how that is not patentable or that we elect not to patent, processes for which patents are difficult to enforce, and information or technology that is not covered by patents.
The Company depends on certain technologies that are sold or licensed to it.
Our success also will depend upon our ability to attract and retain additional qualified management, marketing, technical, and sales executives and personnel.

We rely on information technology systems to keep financial records and corporate records, communicate with staff and external parties, and operate other critical functions, including sales and manufacturing processes.
The prices we receive for our production depend on numerous factors beyond our control.

The declaration and payment in the future of any cash or stock dividends on our common stock will be at the discretion of our Board and will depend upon a variety of factors, including our future earnings, capital requirements, financial condition and such other factors as our Board may consider to be relevant from time to time.
